text:
sara: FYI customer Maya hit a mid-stream silence -> RST when they toggle from office Wi‑Fi to phone hotspot. They get a partial message chunk, then the stream closes. Customer worries they were billed for partial output. App: Android 4.2.1, okhttp 4.x.

maya: repro steps I used: 1) start stream, 2) after ~12s switch to phone hotspot, 3) stream shows some chunks then client reports connection reset. I can reproduce ~7/10.

luis: Can you paste the client debug log (okhttp) + server connection logs? Also need exact request headers. If we can get a tcpdump around the switch that would help. :eyes:

maya: attaching snippets (trimmed):
```
I/EventStream: chunk id=34 bytes=512
I/Network: WIFI -> HOTSPOT switch detected
E/OkHttp: java.net.SocketException: Connection reset by peer
```

sara: From our side I pulled proxy/ingress logs for that customer request_id=rid_98hf: upstream closed with RST, bytes_sent=348. ALB log shows final status "499" at our LB when client closed, but target logs show 200 beforehand. Seems like client or intermediate proxy closed after partial payload.

ops-bot: deploy-bot detected: rollout v2.14.3 at 2024-11-05 03:12 UTC (no related config changes to streaming).

ben: Two likely vectors: 1) NAT/CGNAT IP flip when phone hotspot rebinds and kernel sends RST to existing TCP conn; 2) middlebox (carrier/proxy) resetting idle connections when it sees no data for a bit. We should check ALB/NLB idle timeouts and our tcp keepalive.

luis: Quick checks: can we confirm ALB idle timeout is 60s (default)? customer saw silence ~10–15s then reset, so not ALB default. Could be client TCP stack sending RST on interface change. OkHttp/Android sometimes does abrupt socket close on network change.

ben: Mitigations:
- server: make sure we flush SSE comments/pings more frequently (every 10s) so middleboxes see activity. Use SSE keepalive comment: `:\n\n`
- client: update to okhttp 4.11 which has better network change handling or implement explicit reconnect with resume token in app layer.
- infra: ask eng-sre to check proxies for rewrite/connection tracking limits.

sara: Repro steps for support to validate (customer + internal):
1) Start streaming call from Android device on Wi‑Fi.
2) Wait until you receive first token chunks (~5–8s).
3) Toggle hotspot on phone (Wi‑Fi -> mobile hotspot) while streaming.
4) Observe client logs for `Connection reset by peer` and server ingress logs for RST/half-close.
5) Capture pcap if possible: `sudo tcpdump -w hotpot-switch.pcap host <customer_ip> and port 443`

luis: I tried a quick repro on Pixel 6 emulator w/ mtu 1500, saw same pattern: after network switch kernel emitted RST for the old socket. TCPloss not correlated. Looks client-side.

maya: any quick fix we can try now? Customer on a live call.

ben: Short term: ask customer to enable client heartbeat every 8–10s (SSE comment or small noop event) and to implement reconnect on reset with idempotent resume (if your app layer can handle dedupe). If they can’t upgrade okhttp, try toggling `Connection: keep-alive` -> ensure socket reuse isn't blocked by system.

sara: Billing ask: will partial chunk be billed? Support: tokenization/billing counts what the model produced server-side; if the request was processed and tokens emitted, it's billable even if the client disconnected mid-stream. Flagging billing team if this customer needs credit.

luis: Action items: 
- [ ] get full tcpdump from Maya (sara).
- [ ] confirm okhttp version & try 4.11 (maya).
- [ ] eng-sre check carrier/proxy logs for NAT rebind (ben).
- [ ] consider server-side keepalive ping rollout (ben).

sara: Escalating to eng-runtime and eng-sre @ben @luis — please advise if we should ship a quick keepalive for SSE comments (config flag) and if there are risks for cost/throughput.

ben: I'll prototype a low-risk flag to emit `:\n\n` every 8s for streaming route; shouldn't affect CPU much. Will post perf numbers. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: jira ticket created: INF-4127 "SSE midstream resets on mobile hotspot switch (customer Maya)" link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4127

sara: thanks everyone — I'll keep Maya updated and attach pcap when she uploads.

maya: uploaded pcap + app logs to ticket. Thanks! :pray:
